extracted.intended_audience: theoretical computer scientists and complexity-theory researchers evaluating Deolalikar's P vs NP proof (and similar claimed proofs)
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the technical correctness, conceptual soundness, and applicability of a claimed proof separating P and NP (here: Deolalikar's manuscript), with attention to finite model theory, random k-SAT/statistical physics arguments, and known complexity-theory barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical and notational correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should be free of typos and notational mistakes (e.g., incorrect words, wrong asymptotic notation, wrong indices, missing braces/parentheses, obscured text in figures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix instances listed (e.g., 'Perfect man' → 'Perfect map'; O() vs Θ()/Ω() usages; incorrect parameter counts n2^n → n2^k; missing parentheses and braces; text obscured by figures). Typos that alter mathematical meaning must be corrected; provide an errata and ensure consistent notation across drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of the high-level proof strategy chain
rubrics_metrics.description: Each step of the high-level strategy (vocabulary V, expressibility of SAT as NP-query over V, P-queries expressible by FO(LFP) over V, implication from FO(LFP) expressibility to an LFP-based polynomial-time algorithm, and contradiction with statistical properties of randomized k-SAT) must be rigorously justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state and prove each implication in the chain. The page reproduces Ken Regan's chain; check that the algorithmic ‘tie-in’ actually follows from LFP expressibility, and that the claimed contradiction with randomized k-SAT statistics legitimately applies to the constructed algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation under lifting/projection (lift vs original solution space)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the argument lifts the original n-variable space to a polynomially larger N-variable product space and reasons about factorization/structure there, it must show the relevant properties (e.g., polylog-parameterizability, cluster geometry) are preserved when projecting back to the original solution space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the specific gap noted: the procedure in Sec. 8.3 creates structure on a lift {0,1}^N, but the projected distribution on {0,1}^n may not preserve recursively factorizable form or cluster geometry. Show why directed-acyclic-graph structure or clustering properties survive projection, or modify the argument to operate without relying on dangerous projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order-invariance claims for LFP computations
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that each stage of an LFP computation is order-invariant must be justified; order-invariance of the overall LFP formula does not imply that each iteration stage is order-invariant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to Anuj Dawar's objection: either provide a proof that each stage maintains order-invariance, or reframe arguments to avoid requiring stagewise order-invariance. Cite and address Neil Immerman's related point on order-invariance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction from LFP to Monadic LFP preserves structural properties
rubrics_metrics.description: The reduction used to encode full LFP into Monadic LFP must preserve the properties on which the proof relies (e.g., polylog-parametrizability, bounded-degree Gaifman graph); encoding should not introduce high-arity relations that collapse locality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address Albert Atserias / Steven Lindell critiques: explain how the induction relation/tupling used in the monadic encoding avoids producing relations of unbounded degree or implicit orderings that render Gaifman-graph locality arguments invalid. Provide explicit constructions and bounds on degrees/diameters introduced by the canonical-structure encodings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Hanf–Gaifman locality
rubrics_metrics.description: When invoking locality theorems (Hanf/Gaifman) ensure their preconditions hold throughout the LFP computation and reductions; Gaifman graph properties must not be destroyed by iterations, successor or encodings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify how locality is preserved when encoding k-ary relations, when successor is present, and across O(log n) iterations of the fixed-point computation. If iterations can produce transitive closures or cliques, show how that is prevented or otherwise handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishability from k-XORSAT (XORSAT objection)
rubrics_metrics.description: The argument must identify a step that is specific to k-SAT and fails for k-XORSAT; otherwise the same reasoning would wrongly show k-XORSAT is hard (but k-XORSAT ∈ P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out where the proof uses non-linear or non-algebraic features of k-SAT that are absent in k-XORSAT. If no such step exists, revise the argument to avoid applying equally to linear systems, or explain why XORSAT is excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with error-correcting code constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims about polylog-conditional independence or about the impossibility of large Hamming-distance clusters must not contradict known existence of efficiently decodable error-correcting codes and their bounds (e.g., near Gilbert–Varshamov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to 'harrison' critique: check whether asserted constraints on solution spaces would preclude well-known codes. If they would, reconcile the claim or adjust definitions (e.g., what 'sufficiently many solution clusters' means) to avoid contradiction with coding theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not equate complex solution-space geometry with inherent time complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Complex/interesting geometry of solution spaces (clustering, frozen variables) does not necessarily imply hardness; provide justification for why structure-based arguments separate P from NP rather than characterizing instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address Ryan Williams and others: show why the particular structural property you use is intrinsic to problems in P vs NP distinction rather than an instance-level artifact; rule out trivial transformations (e.g., mapping satisfiable formulas to SAT0) that preserve geometry while making the problem easy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifier-dependence of 'solution space' must be handled
rubrics_metrics.description: The notion of 'solution space' depends on the verifier; if the proof uses solution-space structure, it must either fix a verifier or show the property is verifier-independent (or explain why the relevant verifier is canonical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SAT0 example shows a verifier can trivialize the solution space. Explicitly state which verifier defines the solution space and why this choice is robust (e.g., preserved under plausible reductions) for complexity-theoretic conclusions. Address the objection that P=NP would yield a trivial verifier for SAT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity: distinguish problems versus instances and handle non-uniform models
rubrics_metrics.description: The argument must distinguish between hardness of individual instances and hardness of problems; non-uniform constructions can make single-instance analysis irrelevant for problems in standard complexity classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per Russell Impagliazzo: show that your characterizations apply to entire problems in uniform models, not only to specially constructed instances; explain role of uniformity in avoiding natural-proofs-style obstructions or non-uniform counterexamples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tupling and locality: passing to tuples must not destroy locality
rubrics_metrics.description: Forming k-tuples as single parameters can break locality because tuple-distance is determined by element overlap; the argument must analyze how locality behaves when moving from single elements to tuples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to Thomas Schwentick: provide bounds/lemmas showing that distances between tuples used in the argument faithfully reflect intended locality notions, or avoid tupling techniques that create spurious short distances via shared elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of local operations must be justified
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if individual computation steps are local, their composition may not be; the proof must contain lemmas showing compositions preserve the necessary notion of locality used in later arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit statements/lemmas relating the locality of composed operations to that of their constituents; identify any crucial places where composition could introduce global effects and show how they are controlled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper treatment of least vs greatest fixed points and boundedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed-point logic arguments must correctly handle greatest fixed points, multiple nested fixed points, and boundedness of the universe; hand-waving about 'only LFP' is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address Charanjit Jutla's objection: treat formulas of forms like νx(f(y,x) ∧ g(y,x)); show why greatest fixed points or complex fixed-point iterations do not invalidate arguments, or extend the formalism to cover them rigorously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision in phase-transition terminology and use (clustering vs condensation vs freezing)
rubrics_metrics.description: When invoking statistical-physics notions (clustering/d1RSB, condensation, freezing), use standard definitions and ensure the correct phase is being used in arguments (e.g., freezing is the relevant property for hardness claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mixing concepts (d1RSB vs freezing vs condensation). Cite and align with work by Krzakala, Zdeborová, Moore, Achlioptas–Ricci-Tersenghi, and make clear which mathematically proven results apply and which are conjectural.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address known complexity-theory barriers (relativization, natural proofs, algebrization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any P vs NP proof must consider how it interacts with the three major barriers: relativization, natural proofs, and algebrization, and explicitly show the approach avoids or resolves them where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss each barrier: why relativization may or may not apply (paper focuses on local properties of k-SAT); whether the method falls into 'natural proofs' pitfalls (Razborov–Rudich); and whether algebrization is relevant. If relying on uniformity to escape natural-proofs, make that reliance explicit and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average-to-worst-case separation issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Using average-case (global) properties of solution spaces to deduce worst-case separations is philosophically and technically delicate; the argument must define and defend any average→worst-case steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Terry Tao and Ryan Williams: formalize any barrier relating average-case structure to worst-case complexity, and show why the approach does not fail due to constructions that simulate complex average-case structure in easy problems or vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overreaching conclusions about average-case hardness
rubrics_metrics.description: If the argument implies that there is a poly-time samplable distribution on which k-SAT is hard on average, state and justify those consequences and examine the complexity-theoretic/cryptographic implications (Impagliazzo's worlds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to Cristopher Moore's remark: clarify whether the proof actually implies average-case hardness (and which model of average-case), and discuss consistency with known frameworks (Pessiland, Minicrypt, Cryptomania). Ensure claims are precise and their implications are acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of polylog-parametrizability under reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that problems in P have polylog-parametrizable solution spaces must ensure reductions (e.g., from LFP to Monadic LFP) preserve polylog-parametrizability of typical fibers and related structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make Claim 1.1/1.2 explicit and justify reduction steps. If a reduction does not preserve the structural property needed to apply Hanf–Gaifman locality or similar, either modify the reduction or the claimed property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, sourcing, and objective neutrality in exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanations and claims should be sourced, constructive, neutrally worded, and avoid subjective speculations; contributions should cite prior work and be clear about which statements are conjectural.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As the wiki itself notes: provide sources for new material, avoid personal subjective opinion, and when making leaps in reasoning, mark them clearly as conjectural or supply full proofs/references. This aids peer review and reproducibility.
